subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add the proposed `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` sub-agent lifecycle phases as a core event contract?
rationale: The behavior appears useful for a real agent-workflow failure, but it creates new core lifecycle semantics that affect gateway events, `agent.wait`, session state, SDK normalization, and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Approve refreshed lifecycle contract
options.body: Accept the additive phases and require a current-main implementation with focused source and behavior proof across embedded-agent, subagent, gateway, session, SDK, and docs surfaces.

options.title: Narrow to diagnostics only
options.body: Keep the existing lifecycle contract and instead improve logs/status projections for startup aborts without adding new event phases.

options.title: Defer to root-cause fixes
options.body: Leave the event contract unchanged for now and handle concrete startup-abort causes such as sandbox initialization failures in narrower issues.

recommendation.title: Approve refreshed lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Accept the additive phases and require a current-main implementation with focused source and behavior proof across embedded-agent, subagent, gateway, session, SDK, and docs surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The current decision spans subagent lifecycle and terminal outcome surfaces where this history points to steipete as the strongest routing candidate.
